headline: H.Res. 603 would have formally disapproved of Speaker Nancy Pelosi starting an impeachment inquiry against President Trump without a full House vote, but the House tabled it and it did not pass.
what_it_does: The resolution would have stated the House's disapproval of the Speaker's decision to begin an impeachment inquiry without a debate or vote by the full House on an inquiry resolution. It was raised as a question of the privileges of the House, which lets a member bring a matter to the floor quickly. Because it was tabled or sent to committee, it did not become a formal House position.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the House of Representatives
who_it_affects.how: It would have put on record the House's view on how an impeachment inquiry should be started, which could have shaped how members vote on similar matters.

who_it_affects.group: The President and executive branch officials
who_it_affects.how: It would have expressed disapproval of the impeachment inquiry process, though it would not have changed any legal duty or power they hold.
